summary_hint: CPA letter from <cpa_name>, <cpa_firm_name> (license <cpa_license_number>/<cpa_license_state>), dated <letter_date>: attests <business_legal_name> exists, borrower <client_or_borrower_names> owns <borrower_ownership_percentage>, self-employed since <business_start_date>

typed_core.name: cpa_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — the attesting CPA; third-party independence

typed_core.name: cpa_firm_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — the firm

typed_core.name: cpa_firm_address
typed_core.why: identity — firm location; source reconciliation

typed_core.name: cpa_license_number
typed_core.why: authenticity — verify the CPA is licensed (the letter's whole value is the licensed attestation)

typed_core.name: cpa_license_state
typed_core.why: disambiguator for cpa_license_number — a license number is only meaningful with its issuing state

typed_core.name: license_status_or_verification
typed_core.why: processor/authenticity — active/verified license; supports reliance on the letter

typed_core.name: client_or_borrower_names
typed_core.why: IN-12 (corroboration) — match the client to the borrower (flattened person[] -> primary + _2)

typed_core.name: business_legal_name
typed_core.why: IN-12 (corroboration) — match the entity to the tax returns / K-1

typed_core.name: entity_type
typed_core.why: IN-12 — the self-employment methodology differs by structure (sole prop vs partnership vs S-corp)

typed_core.name: borrower_ownership_percentage
typed_core.why: IN-12 — ownership share used to attribute business income to the borrower

typed_core.name: business_start_date_or_operating_duration
typed_core.why: IN-12 (corroboration) — the 2-year self-employment history

typed_core.name: business_address_and_activity
typed_core.why: identity — business location and nature; corroborates the return

typed_core.name: cpa_client_relationship_start_date
typed_core.why: processor — how long the CPA has served the business; weight of the attestation

typed_core.name: business_existence_assertion
typed_core.why: IN-12 (corroboration) — the CPA's assertion the business exists and is operating

typed_core.name: self_employment_status_assertion
typed_core.why: IN-12 — the CPA's assertion the borrower is self-employed

typed_core.name: income_or_compensation_facts
typed_core.why: IN-12 — any income/compensation facts the CPA states

typed_core.name: business_liquidity_or_withdrawal_impact_statement
typed_core.why: IN-12 / asset use — the common CPA-letter purpose: whether withdrawing funds harms the business (feeds business-liquidity conditions)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the withdrawal-impact statement verbatim: whether pulling assets from the business hurts operations

typed_core.name: scope_limitations_and_disclaimers
typed_core.why: processor — CPA disclaimers ('no assurance', 'for information only') that limit how much the letter can be relied on
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the CPA's scope limitations/disclaimers — many letters explicitly decline to opine on the borrower's ability to repay; that changes how the letter is used

typed_core.name: letter_date
typed_core.why: recency — how current the attestation is

typed_core.name: cpa_signature
typed_core.why: authenticity/execution — the letter must be signed by the CPA

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: classification/version before extraction; a letter is not a form

rejected.name: cpa_phone_email
rejected.reason: contact only; no rule/processor gate; catch-all

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date, expiration_date
rejected.reason: duplicate letter_date; a letter does not expire

rejected.name: signature_blocks
rejected.reason: cpa_signature covers the one signature that matters

rejected.name: services_provided
rejected.reason: narrative list; no IN-12 field to feed; catch-all

encoding_variations: entity_type — no enum coercer; 'Sole Proprietorship', 'Schedule C', 'Single-member LLC', 'Partnership', 'S-Corporation', '1120-S'. Degrade to str; the structure drives the IN-12 method
borrower_ownership_percentage — '100%', 'sole owner', '50/50', 'a 40% member interest'. No percent coercer; degrade to str and keep verbatim
business_start_date_or_operating_duration — 'since 2015', 'operating for over 8 years', 'established March 3, 2015'. May be a duration, not a date; flatten to str
the assertions — existence / self-employment / withdrawal-impact are prose, not checkboxes; degrade the booleans to str and keep the sentence
scope_limitations_and_disclaimers — CPAs increasingly add AICPA-driven disclaimers refusing to opine on solvency/creditworthiness; capture verbatim as it bounds reliance

open_questions.q: Rule-floor derivability — IN-12's how_engine_checks runs a calculator over the tax documents; it names no CPA-letter field. The fields above are the corroboration a human reads
open_questions.recommendation: (a); flag that IN-12 under-specifies the letter

open_questions.q: Boolean/percent/object degradations — existence/self-employment assertions (bool), ownership_percentage (percent), start-date/duration and address/activity (object) all degrade to str
open_questions.recommendation: keep str + prompt hints now; if a rule later gates on ownership % >= 25%, a percent coercer would help

open_questions.q: Multi-borrower letters — a letter may cover two borrowers/co-owners. client_or_borrower_names flattens to primary + _2
open_questions.recommendation: confirm two is enough or promote to a small list if a rule must address owners individually

notes: No existing_extractor for this document type — new schema.

20 typed-core rows — within the 20-25 target. IN-12 corroboration (existence, self-employment, ownership %, entity type, duration) drives most; the CPA-identity/authenticity block ensures the attestation is from a real licensed CPA.
A CPA 'letter' (a.k.a. CPA comfort/verification letter) is free-form prose on firm letterhead — read the letterhead for firm/CPA/license, the body for assertions, the close for date/signature.

PII: no new _PII_FIELDS registration proposed. client_or_borrower_names is a person name at standard sensitivity (identity); the CPA's identity and license are not borrower PII. If a CPA letter states the borrower's SSN or the business EIN, those must be named typed fields and registered — not left to the unmasked catch-all.

cpa_license_number ('authenticity'), license_status_or_verification ('processor/authenticity') and cpa_signature ('authenticity/execution') carry an 'authenticity/execution' rationale that is not one of the five classes; all mapped to processor (validity/authenticity gate) as a best guess — flagged as ambiguity.
